before.label: English
before.title: Ahalya
stanzas: You call the women of stone statues,
I am made of a few leaves, a few flowers, a little pollen, a little earth and a little water.
Turning the curse I endure into rain and lightning, I have shaken my world;
I have led astray the men who came bearing deliverance with the fragrance of my desire.
Sometimes someone's angry roar reaches my ears;
I burst into delirious laughter like a madwoman.
Flower petals cover my creamy body;
I appear still softer, still more supple.
I expand with my self-sufficient existence;
in dreams, so many times, I enjoy royal pleasures.
My veins and smaller veins flare like sunlight with the joy of lovemaking.
You must have seen the dawn sky:
all the sensations of shivering delight
rise and dance in colours like these.
